title: MintLedger
description: The append-only ID mint ledger (ID Naming Specification §8, Registry Directory Specification §5). It records every ID ever minted in a Project, and is itself a FACT — it records what happened, not an inference — so it lives under registry/_meta/mint-ledger.yaml, not under derived/. It is the ground truth the serial `mint` operation reads to allocate the next ordinal for a type code: max(ordinal for type_code) + 1, width-promoted past 999. Because it is append-only, a tombstoned entity's ordinal stays in the ledger forever and is therefore never reminted (ID spec §7). This schema is authored by the ID Mint Ledger runtime (roadmap Phase 5.4), which serializes appends under an OS file lock so concurrent mints never collide (§9). NOTE on header drift: early Projects seeded the ledger without a top-level `version` key; the field is therefore optional here so both the seeded form (`version: 1` + entries) and the older form (entries only) validate.

version.description: Ledger format version. Optional: templates seed `version: 1`; some early Projects omitted it. Absence means the original (v1-equivalent) form.

entries.description: One entry per minted ID, in mint order (append-only). Never rewritten or reordered; a tombstoned entity's entry stays here forever so its ordinal is never reused.

id.description: The minted ID. Matches the frozen ID grammar (ID spec §9): a 3-4 letter type code, a dash, and a 5+ digit ordinal (width promotes past 999...).

type_code.description: The frozen type code the id belongs to (CHR/EVT/ITM/MAG/TEC/TML/…). One monotone ordinal sequence per type code.

minter.description: Who/what performed the mint — an operator id, or the runtime component that executed the human-authorized mint. Records accountability (ADR-009).

status.description: Optional lifecycle marker mirrored onto the ledger entry. Status is normally tracked on the fact record; this field is a convenience for callers holding only the ledger (e.g. `is_tombstoned`). It does NOT affect ordinal reservation — a tombstoned ordinal stays reserved because its entry is never removed, not because of this marker (ID spec §7). Absent on a freshly-minted entry (mint records id/type_code/minted_at/minter only).
